title: Siegel Zeros: The Gap Between Nonvanishing and Effective Lower Bounds
content: The header situates the Siegel zero problem in analytic number theory. Dirichlet's theorem requires L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for non-trivial characters — this is proved. But HOW SMALL can L(1,χ) be? Three levels are known: (1) Nonvanishing: L(1,χ) ≠ 0 (Mathlib); (2) Siegel's ineffective bound: L(1,χ) > C(ε)/q^ε for any ε (ineffective — C(ε) not computable); (3) Conditional GRH: L(1,χ) ≫ 1/log(q) (effective, much stronger). A 'Siegel zero' is a real zero β ∈ (1-c/log(q), 1) of L(s,χ). Its non-existence is equivalent to effective lower bounds. The file formalizes this structure.
mathContext: Dirichlet character $\chi$ mod $N$. L-function: $L(s,\chi) = \sum_n \chi(n)/n^s$. Siegel's theorem: $L(1,\chi) > C(\varepsilon)/q^\varepsilon$. GRH bound: $L(1,\chi) \gg 1/\log^2 q$. Siegel zero: $\beta \in (1-c/\log q, 1)$ with $L(\beta,\chi)=0$.

title: L(1,χ) ≠ 0: The Mathlib Foundation
content: The theorem L_one_ne_zero is a one-line wrapper around Mathlib's LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero. It establishes L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for any non-trivial Dirichlet character χ mod N (N > 0). This is the analytic core of Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions. The Siegel zero question begins exactly here: nonvanishing is proved, but the quantitative version (how far from 0 must L(1,χ) be?) remains open.
mathContext: For non-trivial $\chi$ mod $N$: $L(1,\chi) \neq 0$. Lean: `LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero hχ`. Foundation of Dirichlet's theorem: $L(1,\chi) \neq 0$ for all non-trivial $\chi \Rightarrow$ each AP $\{a+nd : n\geq 0\}$ with $\gcd(a,d)=1$ contains infinitely many primes.

title: Formalizing Siegel Zeros: IsSiegelZero, HasSiegelZero, SiegelZeroConjecture
content: Three definitions capture the Siegel zero problem. IsSiegelZero χ β c hc hN asserts β ∈ (1 - c/log(N), 1) ∧ LFunction χ β = 0. HasSiegelZero says such β exists. SiegelZeroConjecture says no real primitive character ever has a Siegel zero (expected true under GRH, unproved unconditionally). The key type-theoretic challenge is handling the coercion: β is real but LFunction takes complex inputs. The Lean formalization uses LFunction χ β where β : ℝ coerces to ℂ via ofReal.
mathContext: $\text{IsSiegelZero}(\chi, \beta, c) \iff \beta \in (1-c/\log N, 1) \land L(\beta, \chi) = 0$. SiegelZeroConjecture: $\forall N, \chi, c, \neg\text{HasSiegelZero}(\chi,c)$. Equivalently: $\liminf_{N\to\infty} \min_{\chi \bmod N} L(1,\chi) \cdot \log N > 0$.

title: MVT Proof: Siegel Zero Implies Small L(1,χ)
content: siegel_zero_implies_small_L_one is the key structural theorem: if β is a zero of L(s,χ) in (0,1) with derivative bounded by M on [β,1], then ‖L(1,χ)‖ ≤ (1-β)·M. Proof: L(1,χ) = L(1,χ) - L(β,χ) (since L(β,χ)=0), then MVT gives |L(1,χ)| ≤ (1-β)·sup|L'|. In Lean, this uses norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment' with HasDerivAt.comp_ofReal (converting the complex derivative of LFunction χ to its real restriction). The converse no_siegel_zero_gives_lower_bound shows ‖L(1,χ)‖ > 0 via L_one_ne_zero, regardless of Siegel zero hypotheses.
mathContext: MVT: $|L(1,\chi)| = |L(1,\chi)-L(\beta,\chi)| \leq (1-\beta)\sup_{s\in[\beta,1]}|L'(s)|$. If $\beta$ close to 1 (Siegel zero), $L(1,\chi)$ is small. Key Lean API: `norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment'`, `HasDerivAt.comp_ofReal`, `differentiable_LFunction`.

title: Three Deep Axioms: Siegel Theorem, GRH Implication, Landau-Page
content: Three axioms capture deep analytic number theory not in Mathlib. siegel_theorem (1935): for any ε > 0, L(1,χ) > C(ε)/N^ε (ineffective — C(ε) not computable). grh_implies_no_siegel_zeros: under GRH (no zeros with Re(s) > 1/2), L(1,χ) ≫ 1/(log N)^2. landau_page_theorem: at most one conductor N ≤ Q can have a real zero of L(s,χ) in (1-c/log(Q), 1) — the 'exceptional character'. These axioms are formally stated with full type signatures, enabling honest downstream reasoning about what can be derived from each deep result.
mathContext: Siegel (1935): $\forall\varepsilon>0, \exists C(\varepsilon)>0: L(1,\chi) > C(\varepsilon)/q^\varepsilon$ for all real $\chi$. Landau-Page: at most one 'exceptional' $q \leq Q$ has $L(s,\chi_q)=0$ in $(1-c/\log Q, 1)$. GRH $\Rightarrow L(1,\chi) \gg 1/\log^2 q$.

title: GRH Eliminates Siegel Zeros: Location and Monotonicity
content: Part VII has 8 structural theorems. siegel_zero_bounds extracts interval bounds directly. siegel_zero_positive shows β > 0 when c < log(N). siegel_zero_in_upper_half places β in (1/2, 1) when c < log(N)/2 — exactly the region GRH forbids zeros. grh_eliminates_siegel_zeros: any Siegel zero with c < log(N)/2 lies in (1/2,1), but GRH gives no zeros there, contradiction. grh_implies_no_siegel_zeros_large_conductor quantifies: N > exp(2c) implies c < log(N)/2, so GRH eliminates Siegel zeros for all large N. at_most_one_exceptional_conductor applies Landau-Page: two characters with Siegel zeros in (1-c/log(Q),1) must have the same conductor.
mathContext: Chain: $c < \log(N)/2 \Rightarrow \beta \in (1/2,1) \Rightarrow$ GRH contradiction. Quantified: $N > e^{2c} \Leftrightarrow 2c < \log N \Leftrightarrow c < \log(N)/2$. Lean proof: `Real.log_exp` gives $\log(e^{2c}) = 2c$, then `linarith`.

title: The Open Question: SiegelZeroOpenQuestion := ¬SiegelZeroConjecture
content: SiegelZeroOpenQuestion := ¬SiegelZeroConjecture formally captures the open problem: 'do Siegel zeros exist?' The known hierarchy: L(1,χ) ≠ 0 (proved) → L(1,χ) > C(ε)/q^ε (Siegel, ineffective) → L(1,χ) ≫ 1/log^2(q) (conditional GRH). Whether Siegel zeros exist — i.e., whether L(1,χ) can be as small as exp(-c√(log q)) — is OPEN. The open_question_summary (True := trivial) serves as a catalog marker. nonvanishing_implies_no_exact_siegel_zeros: the s=1 case is resolved (L(1,χ) ≠ 0), but the question concerns zeros at β < 1.
mathContext: Open question: $\exists$ sequence $q_k \to \infty$ and $\chi_{q_k}$ with $L(1,\chi_{q_k}) = o(1/\log^A q_k)$ for some $A>0$? Equivalently: does some 'exceptional character' produce $\beta_k \to 1$? Conjectured false (consistent with GRH), unconditionally open.

title: Part VIII: Monotonicity and Completeness Lemmas
content: The final 8 theorems complete the structural picture. siegel_zero_not_one: β ≠ 1 in any Siegel zero (otherwise L(1,χ) = 0, contradicting nonvanishing). siegel_zero_is_LFunction_zero: extracts the zero condition from IsSiegelZero. siegel_zero_region_nonempty: the region (1-c/log(N), 1) is nonempty for large N. has_siegel_zero_mono and not_has_siegel_zero_of_smaller: monotonicity in c (larger c → harder to have a Siegel zero). landau_page_uniqueness: applies landau_page_theorem to get conductor uniqueness. siegel_implies_L_one_pos and grh_bound_implies_L_one_pos: both Siegel's theorem and GRH give ‖L(1,χ)‖ > 0.
mathContext: Monotonicity: $(1-c'/\log N, 1) \supseteq (1-c/\log N, 1)$ for $c' \leq c$, so $\text{HasSiegelZero}(c) \Rightarrow \text{HasSiegelZero}(c')$. Region nonemptiness: $(1-c/\log N, 1) \neq \emptyset \Leftrightarrow N > e^c$. Lean: `Set.nonempty_Ioo`, `div_lt_one`.
